title: Frontend component testing unit integration end-to-end and accessibility
concepts: Tests should verify externally observable behavior at the smallest practical layer. A unit test isolates a function, a component test exercises a UI boundary, and an end-to-end test checks a real user journey in a browser.
React Testing Library encourages DOM queries that resemble how a person identifies content. Prefer accessible role and label queries; use text and test IDs only when they express the intent better.
user-event models an interaction such as typing or clicking, while fireEvent dispatches a lower-level DOM event. Prefer interaction-level simulation for ordinary user flows.
Mocks replace dependencies at deliberate boundaries; over-mocking React internals or implementation details makes tests brittle. Isolate network behavior and assert rendered consequences.

End-to-end tests run in browsers and can verify routing, navigation, layout-dependent interactions, and network integration. Reliable tests isolate data, use resilient locators, wait for conditions, and capture traces for failures.
Accessibility testing combines semantic queries and automated checks with keyboard, screen-reader, contrast, and manual assistive-technology evaluation; no automated tool proves full accessibility.

items: Automated accessibility checks are not a conformance guarantee
The current Testing Library user-event documentation describes v14 and recommends it over the legacy v13 API.

Vitest 5.0 introduced stable performance and Browser Mode trace-view improvements, nested project/config inheritance, and the vitest doctor command; Vitest 5.1 made Browser Mode trace view stable and enabled failure-only capture by default, and added interactive snapshot review and experimental --since-last-run selection.
Check the official migration guide and installed Vite/Node requirements before upgrading; this lesson covers only its named runner API subset.

Playwright 1.65 added Bun test-runner support and notable TypeScript class-field, inert-element actionability, cookie matching, and proxy-credential behavior changes; its current support notice lists Node.js 22, 24, and 26 and says Node 20 is no longer tested.
